Also find GCD of pair (36, 48), and use that result to find GCD of pair (72, 96)." So we need to compute GCD(45,60). Then use that result to find GCD(90,120). But how do we use that result? Possibly they want to note that if GCD(a,b)=d then GCD(k*a,k*b)=k*d? Actually GCD(90,120) = 30. And GCD(45,60)=15. Indeed 90=2*45, 120=2*60, so GCD(90,120)=2*GCD(45,60)=30. Similarly GCD(36,48)=12. And GCD(72,96)=24 which equals 2*12. So we can show that.
